__readme: Run-level parity fixtures for the versioned eval VERDICT POLICY (verdictPolicyVersion 2). OWNED by mcpjam-backend and GENERATED, never hand-edited: `npm run generate:eval-verdict-run-fixtures` computes every expected output with convex/lib/evalVerdictPolicy.ts#aggregateEvalRunVerdict and convex/lib/evalVerdictFinalization.ts (evalV2IterationHasEvaluatorError, evalV2TrialObservation), and `-- --check` fails when the committed bytes differ from what the current aggregator produces. The Inspector SDK copies this file BYTE FOR BYTE to sdk/tests/fixtures/ and asserts its own mirror (sdk/src/contract/verdict-aggregate.ts) against it; neither side re-authors a row. It EXTENDS eval-verdict-policy-parity-fixtures.json (the per-case roll-up), whose sha256 at the time this corpus was cut is recorded under __generator.caseCorpusBaselineSha256. LOAD RULE: keys starting with "__" are annotations; strip them before handing an input to an aggregator. COHORTS: `runs` pairs a resolved validity policy and case inputs with the FULL expected decision (deep equality, including per-rate exclusion tallies and reason order) and with `expectedTrialStatistics`, the REPORT-ONLY per-case statistics convex/lib/evalVerdictPolicy.ts#evalVerdictTrialStatistics derives from that decision (pass@k and pass^k at k = eligible trials, a 95% Wilson interval on the pass rate, and the pooled eligible/passed trials a comparison is sized by), which a mirror must reproduce to the last bit; `refusals` are inputs the aggregator must refuse, with a distinctive substring of the refusal; `evaluatorErrorSignals` pairs iteration metadata with whether the finalization adapter reads it as an evaluator error; `trialObservations` pairs one iteration row (status, result, metadata) with the observation the adapter produces, or a refusal. RE-SYNC: regenerate here, bump __generator.sourceCommit when an output moved, re-pin FIXTURE_SHA256 in tests/convex/evalVerdictRunAggregationParity.test.ts and convex/lib/mirrors.json, and copy the file to the SDK in the matching Inspector PR.

runs.__label: one case, every trial passes
runs.__why: The plain green run: default coverage, every configured trial completed and graded, pass rate 1 against threshold 1.

runs.__label: one case below its threshold
runs.__why: A measured failure: validity holds, so the task verdict decides, and 2/4 is below 0.75.

runs.__label: threshold met exactly at the boundary
runs.__why: The comparison is >=, not >: 2/4 against 0.5 passes.

runs.__label: passThreshold 0 passes any measured case
runs.__why: Zero is a real threshold once something was graded: every trial failing still meets it. Contrast the zero-eligible rows, where no threshold can be met.

runs.__label: passThreshold 1 fails on a single failure
runs.__why: 4/5 is below 1.

runs.__label: fractional pass rates against fractional thresholds
runs.__why: IEEE-754 division is deterministic across both producers: 1/3 meets 0.33 and misses 0.34. One case each, so the run fails on the second.

runs.__label: mixed case outcomes: one passes, one fails
runs.__why: The run verdict is the worst measured case: one failing case fails the run, and the reason is exactly the one the cases produced.

runs.__label: zero eligible: every grader broke
runs.__why: Evaluator errors are never task failures. Nothing was gradeable, so the run is inconclusive and names every validity check that failed.

runs.__label: evaluator errors at the ceiling still hold
runs.__why: 1/10 evaluator errors against the default 0.1 maximum holds (<=); the nine graded trials decide the verdict.

runs.__label: evaluator errors above the ceiling
runs.__why: 2/10 exceeds 0.1, so validity fails whatever the graded trials say.

runs.__label: unreported trials break the default coverage rule
runs.__why: An omitted minEligibleTrials means every configured trial must be attempted. Two configured trials never reported, which is notTerminal, not absence.

runs.__label: cancelled trials are withdrawn from every denominator
runs.__why: A cancelled trial is not an incomplete attempt, but it is not an attempt either, so the default coverage rule still fails.

runs.__label: an explicit minEligibleTrials tolerates unattempted trials
runs.__why: With a declared floor the coverage rule is the floor alone: one eligible trial of three configured holds, and completion is measured over what was attempted.

runs.__label: minEligibleTrials not met
runs.__why: Two eligible trials under a floor of three, and 2/3 completion under 0.8: both reasons, in vocabulary order.

runs.__label: timed-out and failed executions lower completion
runs.__why: Both are attempted but not completed: 3/5 completion is below 0.8.

runs.__label: one timed-out trial within the completion minimum
runs.__why: 4/5 completion meets 0.8 exactly; the four graded trials decide.

runs.__label: setup failures measure nothing
runs.__why: setup_failed is attempted and never completed: zero completion, zero eligible.

runs.__label: nothing attempted: the rates are not measured
runs.__why: pending and skipped never began, so completion and evaluator-error rates are notMeasured (0/0 is never a pass) and every applicable reason is reported.

runs.__label: a running trial is attempted but not complete
runs.__why: A mid-run roll-up: running stays in the attempted denominator, so an unfinished run cannot report full completion.

runs.__label: execution variants: one arm fails
runs.__why: A fan-out case aggregates per (case, provider/model); one failing arm fails the run.

runs.__label: execution variants: one arm never reported
runs.__why: The silent arm keeps its identity and configured trials, so an outage in one provider lowers coverage instead of shrinking the run to the arms that worked.

runs.__label: the same model on two providers are distinct aggregates
runs.__why: Provider is part of variant identity.

runs.__label: variant-keyed and unkeyed cases side by side
runs.__why: One case fanned out (a variant with no provider), another did not; each is its own aggregate and 1/2 meets 0.5.

runs.__label: one unmeasured case among measured ones
runs.__why: Every case must have an eligible trial: c_b only failed setup, so the run is inconclusive although c_a passed and the run-wide rates hold.

runs.__label: validity is decided before the task verdict
runs.__why: The case would pass (3/5 meets 0.5) but completion is 0.6, so the run is inconclusive with validity-only reasons and the case row still records its own verdict.

runs.__label: a strict completion minimum
runs.__why: minCompletionRate 1: a single execution failure is enough to withhold a verdict.

runs.__label: zero evaluator-error tolerance
runs.__why: maxEvaluatorErrorRate 0: one broken grader in five withholds the verdict.

refusals.__label: a completed trial with neither a verdict nor an evaluator error
refusals.__why: Malformed evidence, not an outcome: guessing a reason is how a grader failure becomes a server failure.
refusals.expectedErrorIncludes: neither a task verdict nor an evaluator error

refusals.__why: A trial the run never configured would inflate a denominator.
A status from a newer producer cannot be tallied under any exclusion reason.
The two trial sets would collapse into one denominator.

refusals.__label: one case with both a variant-keyed and an unkeyed aggregate
refusals.__why: An omitted variant means the run did not fan out, never "any variant".
A decision summarizes at least one case aggregate.
refusals.expectedErrorIncludes: needs at least one case aggregate

refusals.__why: v2 thresholds are fractions; 80 is a structural error, never "80%".
configuredTrials is the per-variant repetitions count, within 1..100.

refusals.__label: more configured trials than the portable maximum
an explicit coverage floor of zero
refusals.__why: A declared floor is at least 1; "no floor" is the default coverage rule, not zero.

refusals.__label: a default coverage rule with a different gradeable floor
refusals.__why: minGradeableTrials is pinned to 1 under the default rule.
refusals.expectedErrorIncludes: is pinned to 1 under the default coverage rule

refusals.__label: a caseId outside the opaque-id charset
refusals.__why: The produced decision is self-checked against the same validator that guards a persisted one, so an identity it could not store is refused at production.

refusals.__label: an execution variant with an empty model
refusals.__why: Variant identity needs a model; the self-check refuses what it could not key.
refusals.expectedErrorIncludes: model must be a non-empty string

evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: An older producer that reported nothing has no gating scorer to be missing.
Evidence rejected at the write boundary is a broken measurement whatever the rows say.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: legacy metadata with no evaluation config
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: No definitions declares no gating scorer, so nothing can be missing or broken.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a gating scorer errored under onError fail
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: The grader broke and its author said that is a failure of the measurement.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a gating scorer errored under onError ignore
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: The author already tolerated this outcome; the adapter must not re-add a policy they turned off.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a gating scorer skipped under onSkipped fail
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: "The judge never ran" is its own failure, distinct from a crash.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a gating scorer skipped under onSkipped ignore
a configured gating scorer with no row, onSkipped fail
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: Absence is the unreported form of "never ran"; iterating the rows alone would never visit it.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a configured gating scorer with no row, onSkipped ignore
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: An author who tolerates the reported skip cannot have meant to forbid the quieter one.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: gating scorers declared, no score array at all
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: Resolves through the same missing-row rule, not a second one.
An optional signal breaking is not a measurement failure of what is gated on.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: an advisory scorer produced no row
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: Only gating scorers can be missing.
"required" is canonical and "gating" its legacy spelling of the same value; both gate.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a gating scorer that declared itself not applicable
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: not_applicable is a measurement ("nothing to measure") and counts as represented.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a score row whose scorer has no definition
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: An unattributable row has an unknown role and is not assumed gating.

evaluatorErrorSignals.__label: a gating error with an unresolved onError
evaluatorErrorSignals.__why: Only an explicit onError "fail" makes an error row an evaluator error on this path; resolved definitions always carry the policy.

trialObservations.__label: a completed iteration whose gating grader broke
trialObservations.__why: The evaluator-error signal wins over the recorded result.

trialObservations.__label: a timed-out iteration that recorded a pass
trialObservations.__why: A verdict on a row that did not complete describes grading that never finished; the status is taken verbatim and the result ignored.

trialObservations.__label: a completed iteration still marked pending
trialObservations.__why: Two contradictory statements at once: refused, naming the row.
trialObservations.expectedErrorIncludes: which is neither a task verdict nor an evaluator error
